facts.text: In the federal system the government exists at two levels: the Central Government at the national level and the State government at the regional or State level.
facts.quote: In the federal system, the government exists at two levels. Federal that is the Central Government works at the national level and the State government works at the regional or State level.

facts.text: India has a large geographic expanse and a multicultural population; it could not be governed from one centralised place, so the Constitution adopted a federal setup.
facts.quote: India has a large geographic expanse with a multicultural population. ... It would not have been possible to govern from a centralised place; therefore the Constitution has adopted a federal setup for India.

facts.text: It was decided to form the States on the basis of language; accordingly, linguistic reorganisation of states took place.
facts.quote: It was decided to form the States on the basis of language. Accordingly, linguistic reorganisation of states took place.

facts.text: The nature of government machinery in all states of India is the same; Jammu and Kashmir is an exception.
facts.quote: The nature of government machinery in all states of India is same. However, Jammu and Kashmir is an exception.

facts.text: India has 28 Constituent States but 31 Vidhan Sabhas, because the Union Territories of Delhi and Puducherry and Jammu and Kashmir also have Vidhan Sabhas.
facts.quote: India has 28 Constituent States but there are 31 Vidhan Sabhas. This is because the Union Territories of Delhi and Puducherry and Jammu and Kashmir both have Vidhan Sabhas.

facts.text: Every State has its own legislature, but only seven states in India have two Houses, i.e. bicameral legislatures; Maharashtra has a bicameral legislature.
facts.quote: every State has its own legislature. But only seven states in India have two Houses ie. Bicameral legislatures. Maharashtra has a bicameral legislature.

facts.text: Members of State legislatures are known as Members of Legislative Assembly (MLA) or Members of Legislative Council (MLC).
facts.quote: The members of State legislatures are known as Members of Legislative Assembly (MLA) or Members of Legislative Council (MLC).

facts.text: The Legislature of Maharashtra has two Houses: Vidhan Sabha (Legislative Assembly) and Vidhan Parishad (Legislative Council).
facts.quote: Legislature of Maharashtra has two Houses, namely-Vidhan Sabha (Legislative Assembly) and Vidhan Parishad (Legislative Council).

facts.text: Vidhan Bhavan is in Mumbai.
facts.quote: Vidhan Bhavan, Mumbai

facts.text: The Vidhan Sabha is the first House of the Maharashtra legislature and has 288 members.
facts.quote: This is the first House of the Maharashtra legislature and comprises of 288 members.

facts.text: If the Anglo-Indian community is inadequately represented, the Governor nominates one member from this community to the Vidhan Sabha.
facts.quote: In case there is inadequate representation of the Anglo-Indian community the Governor nominates one member from this community in the Vidhan Sabha.

facts.text: Some Vidhan Sabha seats are reserved for the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
facts.quote: Some seats are reserved for the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.

facts.text: Maharashtra is divided into territorial constituencies for elections, and one member is elected from each constituency.
facts.quote: Maharashtra is divided into territorial constituencies for the purpose of elections. One member is elected from each of the constituencies.

facts.text: The tenure of the Vidhan Sabha is 5 years, but in exceptional circumstances elections can be held before 5 years are completed.
facts.quote: Tenure of Vidhan Sabha is 5 years. However, in exceptional circumstances elections can be held before the completion of 5 years.

facts.text: Any citizen residing in Maharashtra who has completed 25 years of age can contest the Vidhan Sabha elections.
facts.quote: Any citizen residing in Maharashtra and who has completed 25 years of age can contest the elections to the Vidhan Sabha.

facts.text: The proceedings of the Vidhan Sabha are carried out under the supervision and guidance of the Speaker.
facts.quote: The proceedings of the Vidhan Sabha are carried out under the supervision and guidance of the Speaker.

facts.text: The elected members of a newly constituted Vidhan Sabha elect the Speaker and Deputy Speaker from amongst themselves.
facts.quote: The elected members of the newly constituted Vidhan Sabha elect the Speaker and Deputy Speaker of the Vidhan Sabha from amongst themselves.

facts.text: The Speaker prepares the order of business, conducts the House in a disciplined manner and can suspend members for misbehaviour or misconduct.
facts.quote: The Speaker has many responsibilities which range from the power to prepare the order of business, to carry out the proceedings of the House in a disciplined manner, or to suspend members for misbehaviour or misconduct.

facts.text: In the absence of the Speaker, the Deputy Speaker takes over the responsibility.
facts.quote: In absence of the Speaker, the responsibility is taken over by the Deputy Speaker.

facts.text: Maharashtra's legislature holds at least three sessions a year: the budget and monsoon sessions in Mumbai and the winter session in Nagpur.
facts.quote: Maharashtra's legislature conducts minimum three sessions in a year. The budget session and monsoon session is conducted in Mumbai while the winter session is conducted in Nagpur.

facts.text: The Vidhan Parishad is the second House of the Maharashtra legislature; its members are indirectly elected from various sections of society.
facts.quote: It is the second House of the Maharashtra legislature and members are indirectly elected from various sections of society.

facts.text: There are 78 members in the Vidhan Parishad of Maharashtra.
facts.quote: There are 78 members in the Vidhan Parishad of Maharashtra.

facts.text: Some Vidhan Parishad members, distinguished personalities from literature, science and social service, are nominated by the Governor.
facts.quote: some members who are distinguished personalities from the fields of literature, science and social service are nominated by the Governor

facts.text: The remaining Vidhan Parishad members are elected by the members of Vidhan Sabha, local government institutions, teacher-constituencies and graduate constituencies.
facts.quote: remaining representatives are elected by the members of Vidhan Sabha, local government institutions, teacher-constituencies and graduate constituencies.

facts.text: The Vidhan Parishad is never fully dissolved; a specific number of members retire every 2 years and fresh elections fill those seats.
facts.quote: The Vidhan Parishad is never fully dissolved. A specific number of members retire every 2 years and these vacant seats are filled again by conducting fresh elections for those seats.

facts.text: The proceedings of the Vidhan Parishad are under the Chairman; in his absence, the Deputy Chairman takes over.
facts.quote: The proceedings of the Vidhan Parishad are conducted under the control and guidance of the Chairman. In absence of the Chairman, the Deputy Chairman takes over the responsibility.

facts.text: The Governor, the Chief Minister and the Council of Ministers together form the executive of Maharashtra.
facts.quote: The Governor, Chief Minister and the Council of Ministers together form the executive of Maharashtra.

facts.text: The President is a nominal head at the Centre while the Governor is the nominal head at the state level.
facts.quote: The President is a nominal head at the Centre while the Governor is the nominal head at the state-level.

facts.text: The Governor is appointed by the President and holds office during the pleasure of the President.
facts.quote: Governor is appointed by the President and holds the office during the pleasure of the President.

facts.text: Bills passed by the Vidhan Sabha and Vidhan Parishad become laws only after the assent of the Governor.
facts.quote: the bills passed by the Vidhan Sabha and Vidhan Parishad are converted into laws only after receiving the assent of the Governor.

facts.text: The Governor has the right to summon the session of the state legislature.
facts.quote: The Governor has the right to summon the session of the state legislature.

facts.text: When the legislature is not in session but a law is needed, the Governor can issue an Ordinance.
facts.quote: When the legislature is not in session but the need arises to make the law, then the Governor can issue an Ordinance for the same.

facts.text: The leader of the majority party in the Legislative Assembly becomes the Chief Minister.
facts.quote: The leader of the majority party in Legislative Assembly becomes the Chief Minister.

facts.text: Like the Prime Minister, the executive head of the Union, the Chief Minister is the head of the state executive.
facts.quote: Like the Prime Minister who is the executive head of the Union, the Chief Minister is the head of the state executive.

facts.text: The government of the state is run in the name of the Governor, but in reality the administration is carried out by the Chief Minister.
facts.quote: The government of the state is run in the name of the Governor. But in reality, the administration is carried out by the Chief Minister.

facts.text: After proving the majority, the Chief Minister forms the Council of Ministers, accommodating various regions and social groups to make it representative.
facts.quote: After proving the majority, the Chief Minister forms his/her Council of Ministers. This is a challenging task because in order to make the Council more representative, various regions and social groups ... have to be accommodated.

facts.text: If no party gets a clear majority, different parties can come together to form the government, and the Chief Minister must give a place to all parties in the alliance.
facts.quote: If no party secures a clear majority, different parties can come together to form the government. In such case, the Chief Minister has to perform the difficult task of giving a place to all the constituent parties in the alliance.

facts.text: While distributing portfolios, the Chief Minister considers political experience, administrative skills, awareness of public opinion and leadership qualities.
facts.quote: While distributing portfolios, he/she has to consider the political experience, administrative skills, awareness of public opinion, leadership qualities etc.

facts.text: The Chief Minister and the Council of Ministers are collectively responsible to the Legislative Assembly; the Chief Minister bears the ultimate responsibility of efficient administration.
facts.quote: The Chief Minister along with his Council of Ministers are collectively responsible to the Legislative Assembly. The Chief Minister bears the ultimate responsibility of the efficient administration.

facts.text: The Chief Minister resolves conflicts between Departments so they work towards the same goal in the same direction.
facts.quote: Therefore, the Chief Minister has to resolve conflicts between Departments and ensure that they work towards the same goal and in the same direction.

facts.text: Just as the Prime Minister leads the country, the Chief Minister leads the state; people look at the Chief Minister as a problem solver.
facts.quote: Just as the Prime Minister leads the country, the Chief Minister leads the state. ... The people look at the Chief Minister as a problem solver.

facts.text: Maharashtra is one of the progressive States; it leads in sectors like education, industry, service sector, health and social security.
facts.quote: Maharashtra is one of the progressive States in India. The State leads in sectors like education, industry, service sector, health and social security etc.

facts.text: Terror attacks and Naxalite (Left-wing extremist) movements are the two major challenges facing Maharashtra.
facts.quote: Terror attacks and Naxalite (Left-wing extremist) movements active in certain regions are the two major challenges facing the State of Maharashtra.
